title: Catch an AttributeError
description:
Source instruction (Exercises: Day 15, item 1): "Open you python interactive shell and try all the examples covered in this section."

AttributeError example: after `import math`, `math.PI` raises `AttributeError: module 'math' has no attribute 'PI'` ("Instead of pi, I tried to call a PI constant"); fixed by using `math.pi` which returns `3.141592653589793`.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `safe_getattr(obj, attr)`, returning `getattr(obj, attr)`, or a string "AttributeError: <message>" if the object has no such attribute.
examples:
safe_getattr(__import__('math'), 'PI') -> "AttributeError: module 'math' has no attribute 'PI'"
safe_getattr(__import__('math'), 'pi') -> 3.141592653589793
hints: getattr(obj, attr) looks up an attribute on obj by name, the same way obj.attr does, but takes the attribute name as a string argument.
getattr() raises AttributeError when the object has no attribute with that name, just like math.PI did in the source example.
Wrap `return getattr(obj, attr)` in try/except AttributeError, and in the except branch return an f-string starting with 'AttributeError: ' followed by the caught exception object.
expected_behavior: Returns getattr(obj, attr) when the attribute exists. If it doesn't, catches the AttributeError and returns a descriptive string in the form "AttributeError: <message>" instead of letting the exception propagate.

hidden_tests.label: wrong-case constant name, mirrors the source example
valid attribute name returns the value

explanation: getattr() fetches an attribute by name and raises AttributeError if it isn't found. The math module has a lowercase `pi` attribute but no `PI`, so requesting 'PI' raises AttributeError, which is caught and turned into a descriptive string.
